name: Feast Of Jubilee The
overview: The Feast of Jubilee, held every fiftieth year and beginning on the Day of Atonement, is a divinely ordained year of liberty and restoration. Scripture teaches that during this special holy year, redemption of sold property and release of Hebrew servants occur, ensuring that no land is sold permanently since the land ultimately belongs to the Lord. The value of property sales is carefully calculated to allow owners to reclaim their inheritance, emphasizing God's provision for His people as illustrated in the detailed redemption laws. This feast, proclaimed by trumpets, symbolizes the year of the redeemed and illustrates the Gospel by demonstrating God's mercy and the restoration of His people to their rightful place.
